# Command reference

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-codkit-docs.mjs; do not edit by hand. -->

Codkit manages an external patch set and a separate fork tree; which family of upstreams that tree belongs to is the project type's answer (`codkit types`). The public command and flag tables below are rendered from the output of the live CLI; command-flag arity is read from `packages/codkit/src/lib/argv.ts`.

Install the launcher as `codkit` on `PATH`, or invoke the explicit Bash launcher as `<codkit-tool-root>/bin/codkit ...` and the PowerShell launcher as `& <codkit-tool-root>\bin\codkit.ps1 ...`. Never look for a launcher or `package.json` in the patch-set directory. Running the launcher with no arguments prints the current help and exits 0. There is no global `--help`; `codkit imageset --help` is the one command-scoped help and it answers before any root is required, while passing `--help` to another command is a usage error (exit 2).

## Global flags

Global flags are accepted before or after the command name (before a bare `--`).

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--fork-dir <path>` | path of the fork tree (source: flag) |
| `--patches-dir <path>` | path of the Codkit patch-set repository (source: flag) |
| `--json` | machine-readable output on stdout |
| `--ci` | non-interactive mode, no network |
| `--verbose` | diagnostics on stderr |

External paths are independent. Fork-tree resolution is `--fork-dir` → `CODKIT_FORK_DIR` → `~/.codkit/settings.json` `forkDir`; patch-set resolution is `--patches-dir` → `CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR` → the same settings file's `patchesDir`. There is no sibling-directory fallback. Tool, patch-set, and fork roots must be pairwise disjoint. `codkit --json where` is configuration-free and reports the three selected roots and their sources in a schema-2 envelope.

## Commands

The synopsis lists public command flags only. Global flags may be added to every command.

| Synopsis | CLI summary | Operational detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codkit where` | print the resolved fork tree path and the source of that path | Resolve the external roots and report schema-2 `roots.tool`, `roots.patches`, and `roots.fork` with their winning sources, plus the project type the patch set declares. |
| `codkit workspace` | manage named local patchset/fork worktree pairs | Named worktree pair namespace; choose create, list, show, finish or remove. |
| `codkit workspace create <name> [--dir <path>] [--owner <owner>] [--session <identifier>] [--ref <ref>]` | create or resume an isolated worktree pair | Create an isolated patchset task worktree and detached fork pair in an existing --dir parent. --owner and --session are required for a journaled retry; --ref selects the source patchset commit (default HEAD). Source roots use normal --patches-dir/--fork-dir resolution. Registry authority is fixed to ~/.codkit/workspaces.json and must be disjoint from source repositories. Changed partial work or foreign custody refuse without cleanup. |
| `codkit workspace list` | list the user-controlled workspace registry | Inspect the fixed user workspace registry without reading ambient root settings or importing adapters. Explicit external root flags refuse. Missing registry returns an empty versioned registry; removed records remain historical evidence. |
| `codkit workspace show <name-or-UUID>` | show a workspace record by name or UUID | Inspect one registry record by case-insensitive name or exact UUID. No adapter is imported and no checkout is changed. |
| `codkit workspace finish <name-or-UUID>` | seal clean/save proof for a workspace pair | Verify actual checkout receipts and the saved installed type contract before adapter import, then seal clean/save evidence while holding both checkout writer guards. Dirty/unextracted history, stale generated evidence and live/unresolved daemons refuse. Both directories remain present. |
| `codkit workspace remove <name-or-UUID>` | remove a finished pair while retaining its heads and journal | Remove only an unchanged finished pair. Ignored files, unowned empty directories, dirty work, foreign receipts, live writers and submodules refuse. Both heads survive in UUID-scoped repository refs; interrupted deletion retains a removing journal for retry. This command needs no installed adapter. Explicit external root flags refuse. |
| `codkit types` | print the registered project types, their packages and their capabilities | Print the project types this installation carries: the identifier a `codkit.json` may declare, the package that implements it, its version and the capabilities it answers. Needs no patch set. |
| `codkit config` | configuration migration namespace | Configuration namespace; use config migrate for the explicit schema transition. |
| `codkit config migrate [--write]` | preview or explicitly migrate config v2/v3 to v4 | Preview config v2/v3 to v4 with minimal-intervention@1 without importing a type adapter. --write explicitly applies the canonical conversion under the config lock; active operations and changed bytes refuse. Repeating an already-v4 conversion writes nothing. V4 permits pin.tag to be absent; pin.sha remains the immutable revision, pin.date the commit date, resolvedAt the resolution timestamp when known, and provenance declarative source/digest evidence. Ordinary v2/v3 writes preserve their schema. No fork is required. |
| `codkit check-tree [--require-clean]` | check that the fork tree is the upstream tree this patchset tracks | Read-only identity and pin/LFS checks. `--require-clean` also returns 1 when paths outside the own directory are dirty. |
| `codkit clone [--from <url\|path>]` | clone the upstream fork tree into the resolved path and check out the pin | Clone from `--from` or `publishRemoteUrl`, check out the pin, and fetch LFS content. Rejected by `--ci`. |
| `codkit load [--fresh] [--dry-run] [--clone-if-missing] [--discard] [--inputs <working\|pinned>] [--no-inputs]` | bring the fork tree to the pin and apply the delta | Apply the delta at the configured pin. `--dry-run` reports without writing; `--fresh` uses the configured cleanup whitelist and replaces an overlay target that still carries the exact materialization `overlay apply` wrote; `--clone-if-missing` is networked and therefore rejected by `--ci`; `--discard` drops fork-tree commits on purpose (kept reachable under `refs/codkit/consumed/`) and is likewise refused under `--ci`. With `--fresh`, `--discard` also drops the working-tree edits of tracked upstream files that carry no marker block - a build artifact in a dev tree - printing `discard <path>` for each before the first write and reporting them in `data.discardedPaths`; a file with a marker block, own code, own extensions and untracked paths are never dropped. A plain load also passes over a materialized own extension no record declares any more instead of refusing over it: it neither writes into that directory nor removes it, `codkit status` names it, and `--fresh` is what sweeps it. Every other guarded command treats the directory as it did. `--inputs working\|pinned` chooses where the inputs of the configuration come from - the working tree of each input's repository, uncommitted edits included (the default), or its pinned commit - and `--no-inputs` delivers none and leaves the delivered ones as they are; an input lands untracked at its `to`, hidden by the managed exclude block, a build is skipped while the stamp of its content stays the same, and an edit made in an input directory is named and replaced by the input's bytes. |
| `codkit status` | show the pin, the branch, and what is not extracted into patchset yet | Show the pin/generated branch and work in the fork tree that has not been extracted. The own-extension line also counts the stranded materializations - untracked `extensions/<name>/` directories that no record of the manifest declares and the pin does not ship, which only `codkit load --fresh` removes; each is listed with that recipe and raises the exit code to 1. Changed upstream files that are exactly the overlay materialization codkit itself writes are reported in `data.upstream.materializedOverlayTargets`, and when they are the only thing the tree carries the printed next step is `codkit load --fresh` rather than `codkit save`, which is not what withdraws an overlay target. Every input of the configuration is reported: what the tree carries of it, each path edited in its directory (exit 1; the change belongs to the input's repository), and warnings for a pin behind the HEAD of that repository or a repository with uncommitted changes. |
| `codkit save [path ...] [--commit] [--message <text>] [--allow-new-file <path> ...] [--squash]` | extract the changes of the fork tree back into the patchset delta | Extract all changed paths, or only the named paths, back into patchset. Tree commits replay one by one into patchset history with their own subject, author and date plus a `Codkit-Tree-Commit` trailer; `--squash` folds them into one commit, and without tree commits it is a no-op that says so. `--allow-new-file` is repeatable. `--commit` commits the uncommitted remainder; `--message` supplies its message (or the squash subject under `--squash`). An edit in the directory of an input is refused before anything is written: that content belongs to the repository of the input. |
| `codkit sync [--squash] [--commit] [--message <text>] [--discard] [--fresh] [--dry-run] [--abort] [--continue]` | extract the fork tree work and apply the patch set shifts, one run per side | The two-way command: extract the fork tree work and apply the patch set shifts in one run, per target and under a durable transaction. A file both sides changed stops the run with the 3-way materialized as diff3 markers inside the file's codkit block - resolve them by hand, then `sync --continue` finishes the run and `sync --abort` returns everything to the state before it. `--dry-run` prints the classification; `--discard` drops fork-tree commits on purpose (refused under `--ci`); `--squash`/`--commit`/`--message` shape the patchset history and `--fresh` the rebuild (the extraction flags also apply to `--continue`). |
| `codkit gc [--dry-run] [--keep-consumed <n>] [--older-than <days>]` | remove spent runtime state: old consumed refs, crash scratch, dead locks, caches of gone trees | Remove spent runtime state: consumed refs beyond `--keep-consumed <n>` (default 5) that are also `--older-than <days>` old (default 30), crash scratch under `.codkit/tmp`, dead-owner tree locks, apply caches of trees that no longer exist, and generated `.codkit/out` output. `--dry-run` prints the same plan without removing anything; the kept classes - a stopped sync's transaction, pending draft headers, daemon records, a live owner's lock - are named as kept in the plan and never touched. |
| `codkit marker new <tree-file> --id <id> --type <type> --owner <owner> --reason <text> [--category <category>] [--layer <patch\|entry-module>] [--line <n>] [--add-block]` | scaffold a codkit marker block in an upstream file of the tree | Create an empty marker block and pending patch header. `--id`, `--type`, `--owner`, and `--reason` are required; category defaults to `follow` and layer defaults to `patch`. With `--add-block`, only `--id` (and `--line`) are given: it opens another block of an intervention the file already carries, for a graft that is an import line and a call site. |
| `codkit reresolve <tree-file> [--patch <contained-old-patch>]` | replay an old feature patch over the current fork-tree file | Replay a contained old patch over one current tree file; `--patch` selects the source when automatic lookup is not sufficient. |
| `codkit inventory [--diff <ref>] [--md]` | generate the inventory of the delta, and diff it against another state of patchset | Write `.codkit/out/inventory.json`; `--md` also writes Markdown and `--diff` compares with a local patchset ref. The inputs of the configuration are listed with their pinned commits. |
| `codkit verify` | run every integrity check of the delta against the pin and the generated branch | Read-only full delta integrity report. The hook-only `--staged-fast` flag is intentionally not public. |
| `codkit overlay new <target> --id <id> --type <type> --owner <owner> --reason <text> [--category <category>] --contract-test <guard-test-id> ...` | scaffold an overlay artifact for a target of the config-overlay layer | Scaffold the artifact of the config-overlay layer for a target: canonical metadata in the schema key order, the pin of `codkit.json`, the guard tests of `--contract-test` (repeatable and required - the layer leaves no marker in the target file, so the test is the only thing that fails when upstream moves the key) and an empty list of operations to fill in. The metadata is held to the vocabularies of `marker new`; an existing artifact of the target is never overwritten. No fork tree is needed, and there is no `--layer`: the artifact is the layer. |
| `codkit overlay apply <target\|overlay-file>` | materialize an overlay target into the fork tree (packaging, CI, publish) | Materialize the composed overlay target for packaging, CI, or publish. |
| `codkit overlay check <target\|overlay-file>` | check an overlay against the pin and against the file in the tree | Check overlay expectations and any materialized tree target without applying it. |
| `codkit build up [--channel <name>]` | start the watch daemons of the fork tree in the background | Start configured watch channels under a short-lived per-channel operation lock, with an exclusive complete reservation; starting/unknown records refuse and a busy channel refuses without touching its record. `--channel` selects one channel. |
| `codkit build down [--channel <name>]` | stop the watch daemons of the fork tree | Stop each proven watcher process group under the same per-channel operation lock and retire only its exact record after every member exits; starting/unknown records, and records owned by another fork tree, refuse without a signal. `--channel` selects one channel. |
| `codkit build status [--channel <name>]` | report which watch daemons are living, by probing their processes | Report starting/living/dead/unknown watcher truth, including descendants left after an npm leader exits; `--channel` selects one channel. It is read-only and point-in-time: exit 0 means the observation succeeded, not that every daemon is healthy, and a record owned by another fork tree is reported as `unknown` with that tree named. |
| `codkit build errors [--channel <name>] [--mine] [--timeout <seconds>]` | wait for the current compilation pass and print its errors | Wait for the current proven daemon pass and print its errors. Starting/unknown state never certifies an old log, and neither does a record whose generation rotated while the log was read or whose tree is not this one; `--mine` narrows channels and `--timeout` is positive seconds. |
| `codkit cycle <start <tag-or-sha> \| continue \| status \| restart> [--yes]` | upgrade cycle: start <tag-or-sha>, continue, status, restart --yes | In config v4, a full SHA target stays unlabelled and operational names use sha- plus the full SHA; a tag target retains its label. Config v2/v3 retain their original tag-selection rules. `restart` alone accepts and requires `--yes`. Exit 3 is a deliberate stop for human input. |
| `codkit forecast [--ref <ref>]` | classify the complete delta against a local future upstream ref | Classify against a ref already present in the fork tree. It never fetches; `--ci` requires an explicit `--ref`. |
| `codkit rebase-onto-pin` | replay feature-only patches after merging a target patchset branch | Replay feature-only patches after the target patchset branch, with its new pin, has been merged. |
| `codkit ci [--profile <verify\|build>] [--effective-diff <base-ref>] [--pin-guard-base <ref>] [--timeout <seconds>]` | run the container threshold: fresh apply, verify, guards, and (with --profile build) one compilation pass | Run the no-network container threshold. Profile defaults to `verify`; `build` additionally requires supplied tree `node_modules`. Pin-guard/effective-diff refs must already exist locally. Every input is built from its pinned commit and committed on the generated branch; the effective diff leaves the directories of the inputs out. |
| `codkit package [<selector>] [--keep-overlay] [--skip-type-build] [--timeout <seconds>] [--inputs <dir>] [--container-prefix <name>] [--component-id <identifier>]` | build the distributable from the loaded tree and put the tree back | Build the distributable out of the already loaded tree: the drift guard of `load`, then the overlay targets materialized into the tree, the stamps the project type names put into the environment, the package build of the type, the packaging step the patch set declared, and finally the targets this run materialized put back and the dev channel rewritten. `<selector>` is a target of the type's catalog, a platform family (`windows`, `linux`, `macos`) or `all`; without it the patch set's default targets are built. Each target runs on the route its type answers for this host - natively in the tree, or in the type's container over a read-only view of the tree, whose artifacts are copied back into it - and a target with no route here is refused with the reason the type gives (`CK-E-CONFIG`). The inputs the targets download are checked first: `--inputs <dir>` names the pre-provisioned copies, and the global `--ci` makes the run offline, so a missing input, or a container image that is not there, is `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN` before any write. `--container-prefix <name>` is the first word of the names of the container route's image, volume and container (default `codkit`). `--keep-overlay` leaves the overlay targets materialized for a hand check (`codkit load --fresh` takes them back); `--skip-type-build` runs only the product step over a tree the watch channels already built; `--timeout <seconds>` bounds each command. Where the artifacts land is the answer of the type and of each target, and a raw bundle written beside the managed tree names none. A failing command is exit 1 `CK-E-PACKAGE-FAILED` with the tail of its output; there is no `--discard`. After successful restoration package emits an immutable component release descriptor with actual artifact hashes, Git/config/type/recipe/policy bindings and explicit missing distribution evidence. `--component-id <identifier>` sets stable component identity; shallow patchset histories require it. When fixed codkit.licensing.json is present, its profile ID selects the trusted user organization store and exact canonical NOTICE/SBOM, source provenance and required delivered carriers are gated before recording success. Invalid or changed declarations/store and stale attachments refuse; the component ID must agree with the declaration. Absence keeps organization evidence explicitly missing. |
| `codkit publish <immutable-patchset-ref> [--profile <verify\|build>] [--release <semver>] [--branch <name>] [--squash] [--orphan] [--author <name-and-email>] [--message-file <path>] [--scrub] [--no-lfs] [--export-bare <dir>] [--export-repo <dir>] --yes-i-am-publish-bot [--component-id <identifier>]` | publish one checked immutable patchset commit through a leased release ref, or into a new local repository | Release-bot-only transaction. It requires `--yes-i-am-publish-bot` and rejects global `--ci`; into `publishRemoteUrl` it gates with `ls-remote` before mutation, and only then checks and pushes leased/immutable refs. `--branch <name>` names the release branch instead of `codkit/release/<patchset12>+<pin-key>` (the label when present, otherwise sha- plus the full SHA), outside the prefixes of the patch set. Three forms of the history: without `--squash`, the pin's history and the generated commits, one per artifact and input, with the Codkit trailers; `--squash` publishes one commit on the pin whose tree is the checked tree, with `--author` as author and committer and the UTF-8 `--message-file` as its message, dated like the patchset commit and without Codkit trailers; `--squash --orphan` writes that commit without a parent - one commit for the whole product, which a push into an empty repository carries without upstream history. The `--release` tag names the published tip. `--scrub` (with `--squash`) removes the codkit marker lines and the `spec://` references of comment lines from the delivered files, and the bare references the patch set learns from itself - its intervention ids and the ids of its spec documents under `publish.scrub.specRoots` (default `vibevm/vibespecs`), plus `publish.scrub.vocabulary` - as whole groups in comment text and Markdown prose: a parenthetical of references, a sentence of them, a leading group with its colon, a group after a preposition. It leaves out the files `publish.exclude` names, and refuses to push while `codkit:begin`, `codkit:end`, `spec://` or `vibevm` is left anywhere in the tree, or a learned reference in any delivered file. `--no-lfs` publishes a tip that needs no git-lfs: it leaves out every path the tree's own `.gitattributes` give to `filter=lfs` whose blob is a pointer, and removes each rule that names `filter=lfs` with the comment lines directly above it - in the squashed tree, or as one more generated commit, `codkit: leave out git-lfs content`, without `--squash`; a tree without git-lfs content stays as it is, and a rule the rewrite does not remove, such as a macro, stops the run with `lfs-failed` before anything is written. `--export-bare <dir>` or `--export-repo <dir>` writes the release into a new bare repository, or a new repository with the branch checked out, instead of `publishRemoteUrl`, which is then neither required nor read - no gate, no push, no network. The directory must be new or empty, with an existing parent, outside the patch set and the fork tree; the repository gets the branch, the release tag and only the objects the tip reaches, with no remote and no alternates, `core.longpaths=true`, and `core.autocrlf=false` with `core.eol=lf` for a working tree that plain git sees clean. Unless `--no-lfs` is given, the export carries the git-lfs objects of the tip, copied from the lfs storage of the fork tree and checked against their pointers; a missing object is `CK-E-LFS` before anything is created. A failed run leaves no export behind, and a second run into the same directory is refused. The inputs of the patch set enter the release from their pinned commits: one commit each on top of the history, part of the one commit under `--squash`, and scrubbed and searched like every file the patch set adds; the result names each input with its commit and file count. Successful publish emits an immutable descriptor binding the selected patchset commit, checked generated tip and delivered Git objects. Delivery is historical evidence; missing organization policy/notices/SBOM stay explicit. `--component-id <identifier>` selects stable identity for shallow history. A present codkit.licensing.json is read from the selected immutable patchset commit. Licensing inspects a temporary checkout of the shaped delivered tip before push/export, with git-lfs required for hydrated LFS evidence; changed snapshot bytes, canonical documents or selected authority refuse. No declaration keeps missing organization evidence explicit. |
| `codkit inputs <pin>` | namespace of the inputs other repositories build; run inputs pin | A namespace, not a command: bare `codkit inputs` prints its subcommand and exits 2 before any root is resolved. The inputs themselves are declared in the top-level `inputs` list of `codkit.json`. |
| `codkit inputs pin [name ...] [--all]` | move the pin of inputs to the HEAD of their repositories, refusing uncommitted content | Move the pin (`ref` in `codkit.json`) of the named inputs, or of every input with `--all`, to the HEAD of each input's repository, rewriting `codkit.json` canonically. A repository with uncommitted changes is refused with its paths before anything is written, because a pin names committed content; commit the new pin together with the change that needs it. |
| `codkit hooks <install \| check>` | install or check the patchset git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg) | Install or inspect effective Codkit-owned patchset hooks. Check is green only when Git demonstrably executes the current owned bytes; linked/custom/foreign hook paths are inactive refusals. |
| `codkit imageset <gen \| index \| verify> [--help]` | namespace of the product icon set; run imageset gen, index or verify | A namespace, not a command: it never generates. Bare `codkit imageset`, and any unknown subcommand, print the subcommand list and exit 2 before any root is resolved. `--help` lives here and answers the tools question for the whole namespace: none are required, on every supported OS, with the linked libraries and their licences listed so the claim can be checked. |
| `codkit imageset gen [--dry-run] [--branding-dir <path>]` | regenerate the product icon set from branding masters into the resource layer | Regenerate the product's brand images from the branding masters in `<patchset>/branding` (`--branding-dir` overrides) - the application icon, the Windows installer bitmaps, the web client's icons, one drawing per registered file type and the empty-editor watermarks. The first run seeds that directory with the fork tree's own artwork; `<key>.svg`/`<key>.png` masters serve every size and a per-size `<key>-<N>.png` override wins verbatim, where `<key>` is the family for a family holding one drawing and `<family>/<artwork>` for one holding several. Output lands in the resource layer - `delta/resources/files/` plus `map.json` entries - for `load` to materialise; a vector target is emitted unchanged rather than rasterised. `--dry-run` prints the plan, including which master serves each frame, and writes nothing; it reads every master the run would read, so a master the run would refuse, or a per-size override of the wrong size, fails the plan the way it fails the run. A frame a vector master renders at an aspect other than its own is still delivered at the exact size, and the plan, the run, a warning line and the `--json` fields `stretched` and `stretchPercent` all say how far it is stretched from the master's aspect. A PNG master with 16 bits per channel is reduced to 8, and the plan, the run and the `--json` field `reducedFrom16Bit` say so. A drawing without a master is skipped with a warning and exit 1; a new map entry needs its `guard.brand.<family>` suite declared under `delta/own/test/` first - one suite per family, not one per drawing. What the shipped files cannot say, the product declares in `imageset.json` in the masters directory: the frame set of a target whose container allows one - the frames written in place of those the shipped file carries - and `sources`, rules that give the frames of some sizes to another master key (`{"key": "taskbar", "maxSize": 64}`, or explicit `sizes`). A declaration that cannot be applied exactly is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` before anything is read or written; every frame is reported with its key, its master and its origin - in `--json` as `key`, `keyDeclared`, `master` and `origin` - and a patch set without a declaration gets exactly the files it got before. |
| `codkit imageset index [--branding-dir <path>]` | report the icon set: every required size and the master it comes from | Read-only index of the image set, computed from the distribution and the masters directory rather than written down: a per-family summary, then per target its role and container, the exact sizes the distribution requires, and for each size whether it comes from a hand-made master, is generated from a base master, or has no master at all - and, for a size a vector master renders, how far it is stretched from the master's aspect, for a size a 16-bit PNG master serves that it is reduced to 8 bits per channel, and for the size `gen` would skip the target at, the reason `gen` gives. A declared frame set is listed with the frames the shipped file carries, and a size a rule of the declaration gives to another key says so. It reads every master `gen` would read and writes nothing - not even the seeding `gen` does; it exits 0 whether or not masters are missing, and 2 with the refusal of `gen` when `gen` would refuse a master or the declaration. Markdown by default; `--json` carries the same model structurally. |
| `codkit imageset verify [--branding-dir <path>]` | round-trip every layered target against itself and check the acceptance bands | The acceptance bands as an executable gate, run against the distribution the fork tree already holds. For every raster target the largest layer of a container becomes the master, the other layers of that same container are regenerated from it through the pipeline `gen` uses, and each is compared with the layer the distribution ships: structure exactly, pixels within the band of their size range - at most 10/255 mean absolute RGB difference from 256 px up, at most 25/255 from 64 px, nothing asserted below that. The master is always a layer of the same file, so no flag can make it compare one container with another; a target with a single layer has no round trip and is reported as unverifiable rather than counted as passed. A target of the declaration in the masters directory is verified against it: its file must carry the declared frames - a missing or an extra frame is a structural failure - and its layers are round-tripped one master key at a time, so a layer of one drawing is never measured against another. Read-only: no lock, nothing written to the patchset, nothing written to or seeded into the masters directory. Exit 0 when every asserted comparison is inside its band, 1 when one is outside, 2 when the tree or a container cannot be read. Markdown by default; `--json` carries the same model structurally. |
| `codkit license <check \| consumer-check \| annotate \| notices>` | namespace of the licence markup; run license check, annotate or notices | A namespace, not a command: bare `codkit license` and any unknown subcommand print the subcommand list and exit 2 before any root is resolved. The subcommands are `check`, `annotate` and `notices`, and none of them needs a patch set or a fork tree. |
| `codkit license check [<dir>]` | check that every file of a package states its copyright and licence | Check the licence carriers of a package directory the way REUSE reads them: every file resolves to a carrier - an adjacent `<file>.license` sidecar, a `REUSE.toml` annotation, or a header in its first 20 non-empty lines (copyright lines are read up to the `SPDX-License-Identifier` line). An own file (every holder in the policy) must carry a year and exactly `UPL-1.0`; a third-party file must be covered by a `REUSE.toml` annotation that agrees with its carrier, and its licence must be on the policy allowlist. `LICENSE`, one `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` per licence in use, the manifest `license` field and a current `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` are required. Without `<dir>` it checks the standards package codkit ships. Read-only, needs no root, never calls git. Exit 0 clean, 1 with one line per problem (`CK-E-LICENSE-HEADER` per carrier, `CK-E-LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY` per third-party rule, `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE` for the package), 2 when the directory, the policy or the SPDX list cannot be read. |
| `codkit license consumer-check <dir> [--profile <verify\|build>]` | check consumer source against a trusted organization profile | Inspect consumer source read-only against --profile <id> from the trusted user ~/.codkit/organization-policies.json. Requires a resolved patchset root for policy containment, but no fork, configuration or adapter. Source, carrier and policy hashes bind the versioned JSON report. Exit 0 means complete source evidence, 1 incomplete evidence, 2 invalid invocation or unavailable policy. This checks evidence under the selected policy; it does not assert a legal ruling. |
| `codkit license annotate <path ...> [--dir <path>] [--year <YYYY>] [--holder <name>] [--license <spdx-id>] [--source <text>] [--third-party] [--dry-run]` | give files a licence header or a .license sidecar, idempotently | Give files a licence carrier: for an own file a four-line header in the comment style of its extension, placed after the prelude (shebang, `<?xml?>`, encoding line, doctype, front matter), or a `<file>.license` sidecar for binaries and comment-less formats; with `--third-party --holder <name> --license <SPDX-ID> [--source <text>]` a carrier with the other party's holder and licence plus an annotation appended to `REUSE.toml` (the licence must be on the allowlist and an SPDX identifier). `--dir` names the package root (default `.`); a path outside it is refused. `--year` and `--holder` default to the current year and the first policy holder. Idempotent: a file that already resolves to a carrier is reported `unchanged`, so a second run leaves `git diff` empty. `--dry-run` prints the plan and writes nothing. Never downloads a licence text: put `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` in place yourself. |
| `codkit license notices [--dir <path>] [--dry-run]` | generate THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md from the REUSE.toml registry | Generate `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` from the `REUSE.toml` registry of the package named by `--dir` (default `.`): one table row per third-party annotation, in the order the registry lists them. Writes only when the bytes would change (`written` / `unchanged`), removes the file when the registry declares no third-party row, and `--dry-run` prints the generated body on stdout instead of writing - which is what makes `codkit license notices --dry-run \| diff - THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` a check anyone can run. `license check` reports a hand-edited or outdated notices file as stale. |
| `codkit standards <load \| check \| license>` | namespace of the shipped packages; run standards load, check or license | A namespace, not a command: bare `codkit standards` and any unknown subcommand print the subcommand list and exit 2 before any root is resolved. `load` and `check` work on the whole set of packages codkit ships and need only the patch-set root - no fork tree, no codkit.json, no tree lock; `license` needs no root at all. |
| `codkit standards load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` | deliver the packages codkit ships into the patch-set repository | Deliver every package codkit ships into the patch-set repository in one run - `standards`, the norms, and `agent-skills`, the skills `vibe skill install` projects into every coding agent - `standards` first and the rest by name: a byte-for-byte copy of each under `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/<name>/v<version>/`, the codkit licence notice `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` in the repository root and in `delta/own/codkit/` (from where `codkit load` carries it into the fork tree as a file codkit delivers; `codkit publish` leaves it out of the release branch), rendered with a components block that lists what is installed (an edition-2 copy at `delta/own/` is moved), one managed block in the product `vibe.toml` (between `# codkit:begin standards` and `# codkit:end standards`) with one `[requires.packages]` table per package, each pinning its exact version with `link = "static"`, and - when `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` exists - a managed block in it (between `# codkit:begin scrape` and `# codkit:end scrape`) with the two rows that remove the notice from a `vibe scrape` export; without a contract it says so and writes nothing there. The licence check runs first, over every package, and a failing package is never copied - there is no bypass flag, and one failure stops the whole run before the first write. An installed copy that differs from the shipped one is refused with `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT`, the package name and the list of changed paths; a malformed block or an entry outside it is `CK-E-CONFIG`; nothing is written on any refusal. `--upgrade` is the word that takes the shipped copy instead: it prints the `replace` and `remove` paths, swaps the whole package directory through a temporary directory and a rename, drops the version directories the shipped edition supersedes, and makes the next step `vibe install --offline --force` - an edition may be extended in place under the same version number, and codkit cannot tell that from an edit of yours. An edited `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copy is refused even then; delete the copy and run again. Codkit does not run `vibe`: the next steps it prints are `vibe install --offline` and, when a delivered package declares skills, `vibe skill install`, followed by a four-line licence note and the recommendations for the notice file (its full text is printed when a copy was created; `codkit standards license` prints it any time). A repeat is `up to date` with no byte changed. `--dry-run` prints the same plan and exit code without writing. |
| `codkit standards check` | report on the installed packages, the notice files and both blocks | Read-only report on every installed package: whether each copy is absent, identical to the shipped package or drifted (with the package name and the paths), whether its licence carriers are intact, whether the two `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copies (repository root and `delta/own/codkit/`) are identical to the notice rendered for this repository (a copy whose components block is out of date is `stale`, a legacy copy at `delta/own/` is a warning), whether the managed block in `vibe.toml` is absent, current, stale, malformed or shadowed by an entry outside it, and the same for the scrape-contract block (a missing contract is reported as information, not as a finding). Exit 0 only when every copy and both notice files are identical, the licence check is clean and both blocks are current (or the contract is absent); 1 otherwise, one line per finding; the hint for a drifted copy names `codkit standards load --upgrade`, for an edited notice copy `delete the copy and run codkit standards load`, and otherwise `run codkit standards load`. `--json` adds `data.packages: [{name, version, target:{state, paths}}]`. |
| `codkit standards license` | print the codkit licence notice, the recommendations and the scrape rows | Print, needing no root: the full text of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` - the notice a delivering command places in the repository root and in `delta/own/codkit/`, with an empty components block here - then the recommendations (where the copies live, that nobody edits them, that linking to them is the product owner's choice, where the three licence scopes end), the scrape-contract rows that `standards load` keeps in `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` (paste them only into a contract kept elsewhere), and a `REUSE.toml` annotation naming the four paths the notice describes, for the product's own registry. `--json` returns `file`, `text`, `recommendations`, `scrapeContractRows` and `reuseAnnotation`. |
| `codkit runtime <load \| check>` | namespace of the codkit runtime library; run runtime load or check | A namespace, not a command: bare `codkit runtime` and any unknown subcommand print the subcommand list and exit 2 before any root is resolved. Both subcommands need only the patch-set root - no fork tree, no `codkit.json` to run, no tree lock; the pin is read only for the compatibility warning. |
| `codkit runtime load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` | deliver the codkit runtime library codkit ships into delta/own/codkit/ | Deliver the Codkit runtime library - the feature-flag service, the features host and the brand engine - into `delta/own/codkit/` of the patch set, from where `codkit load` carries it into `<ownRoot>/codkit/` of the fork tree, the own root the patch set declares in `typeConfig`. It is a managed copy: the product never edits it, the copy is compared byte for byte with the shipped version, and drift refuses with `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` and the list of paths before anything is written. `--upgrade` replaces the directory as a whole and prints what it replaces and removes - Codkit keeps no older version, so there is nothing to merge; `--dry-run` prints the same plan and writes nothing. The library's own licence check runs first and a failing library is never copied (`CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE`, exit 2), and a shipped tree that is not exactly one version directory whose `common/version.ts` literal matches its name is `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`. The `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copy inside the target directory belongs to `standards load` and is carried across a replacement; both notice copies are rewritten with a components block that now lists the runtime. The run ends with three next steps: the single import for the product's composition root, the `code-import-patterns` block to take from the library's `LAYERS.md`, and `codkit gen feature`. A pin outside `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM` is a warning, not a refusal. A repeat is `unchanged` with no byte written. |
| `codkit runtime check` | report on the installed runtime library and the licence notice copies | Read-only report on the installed runtime library: `runtime not installed` when `delta/own/codkit/` is absent (exit 0), `identical` when it matches the shipped library, or `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` with every modified, extra and missing path and the hint `run codkit runtime load --upgrade` (exit 1). It also reports the state of both `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copies - an edited copy is `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT`, an out-of-date components block is reported without being a finding - and warns about a legacy copy at `delta/own/`. |
| `codkit gen <feature \| brand>` | namespace of the product skeletons; run gen feature or gen brand | A namespace, not a command: bare `codkit gen` and any unknown subcommand print the subcommand list and exit 2 before any root is resolved. Both subcommands write into `delta/own/` of the patch set and need no fork tree. |
| `codkit gen feature <id> --title <text> [--setting] [--cold] [--holder <name>] [--license <spdx-id>] [--year <YYYY>] [--header-style <line\|block>] [--header-file <path>]` | write the skeleton of a flag-gated product feature into delta/own/ | Write the skeleton of a flag-gated product feature: `delta/own/contrib/<name>/common/<name>.ts` with the feature id (and the setting id under `--setting`), `delta/own/contrib/<name>/browser/<name>.contribution.ts` with a `Disposable` subclass and the `registerFeature` call the runtime library reads, and `delta/own/contrib/<name>/test/browser/<name>.test.ts` - the test lives inside the feature, so one unit covers the code and the test alike. The id must be two or more dot-separated camelCase segments (`acme.smartPaste`) or the run is `CK-E-GEN-ID` (exit 2); its last segment names the directory. `--cold` declares `hotToggle: false`, so the flag is frozen at startup and a change asks for a restart. The files are product code: `--holder` and `--license` (with `--year`, defaulting to this year) head them in the style `--header-style` names - `line`, four `//` lines, or `block`, the ruled comment upstream files carry, so own code sits flush with the code beside it. `--header-file <path>`, a path inside the patch set, writes a header the fields cannot express verbatim instead, and the file must end with a newline; it does not combine with `--holder`, `--license`, `--year` or `--header-style`, and `--header-style` without `--holder` and `--license` has nothing to shape - either combination is exit 2 with nothing written. Without any header flag the files are written without a header and the run warns `no header written` - Codkit's own notice is never placed in a product file. An existing target is `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS` (exit 1) and nothing is written at all. The run prints the import line for the product's composition root and the reminder to declare the one unit in `delta/own/patchset.delta.json`. |
| `codkit gen brand [--holder <name>] [--license <spdx-id>] [--year <YYYY>] [--header-style <line\|block>] [--header-file <path>]` | write the brand rules table and print the graft for the distribution's string funnel | Write `delta/own/common/brand.ts` - the product's brand rules table with one worked example and the `except` explanation, exporting `brandMessage` built by the runtime library's `createBrandTransform` - and print the graft for `_format` in `src/vs/nls.ts`, which the product writes itself as a patch with `type = hook`. Two reminders come with it: the hook budget (at most three lines of code between the markers, one of them naming own code) and the `code-import-patterns` target for `src/vs/{monaco.d.ts,nls.ts}`, which has to allow the own root's `common/~`. Headers follow the same rule as `gen feature`; an existing file is `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS` (exit 1). |

## Exit status and output

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Command completed and requested checks passed. |
| 1 | The command ran, but a check/conflict/integrity verdict is red. The reported problem is normally actionable in the repositories. |
| 2 | Usage, configuration, dependency, repository, permission, or other environment/startup failure. Unknown commands/flags are codeless usage errors on stderr and do not produce a JSON envelope. |
| 3 | The upgrade cycle reached a deliberate human decision point. Do not automate past it. |

With `--json`, an invoked command writes one versioned envelope to stdout. Human progress and diagnostics remain on stderr. Require `codkit.schema == 2`; inspect `roots.tool`, `roots.patches`, `roots.fork`, `ok`, `exitCode`, `errors[].code`, and the command-specific `data`; do not parse human prose.

## Network boundary

- Global `--ci` is non-interactive and forbids Codkit network operations. The `ci` command implies the same restriction even when `--ci` is not typed.
- `clone` and `load --clone-if-missing` are the local, explicit ways to obtain a missing tree; both are rejected in `--ci` mode.
- `forecast`, `check-tree`, and `ci` use only objects/refs already present locally. The CI wrapper must provide missing refs, LFS objects, and dependencies.
- `publish` is intentionally not a CI-mode command. It is the only release push path, requires the bot confirmation flag, and refuses the combination with `--ci`. An export into a new local repository (`--export-bare`, `--export-repo`) reaches no network and pushes nothing, and keeps both refusals.

See [conventions](conventions.md), [failure guidance](faq.md), and the [air-gapped supply-kit contract](../ci-examples/air-gapped-supply-kit.md).
